k: Where Evernoon stood there is only the shard, and the wall, and a quiet morning under the new sun. The golden afternoon is gone. Nobody misses it as much as they thought they would.
src: 'Where Evernoon stood there is only the shard, and the wall, and a quiet morning under the new sun. The golden afternoon is gone. Nobody misses it as much as they thought they would.'

k: The dancer smiles at you. Somewhere, faintly, a clock is ticking.
src: 'The dancer smiles at you. Somewhere, faintly, a clock is ticking.'

k: Lemonade! Fresh lemonade! And... swords, apparently. I don't remember stocking swords. I don't remember stocking anything.
src: 'Lemonade! Fresh lemonade! And... swords, apparently. I don\'t remember stocking swords. I don\'t remember stocking anything.'

k: Funny. Same lemon. I've been squeezing the same lemon all afternoon.
src: 'Funny. Same lemon. I\'ve been squeezing the same lemon all afternoon.'

k: Lovely afternoon. Lovely.
src: 'Lovely afternoon. Lovely.'

k: I keep meaning to go home for supper. Mira will have the soup on.
src: 'I keep meaning to go home for supper. Mira will have the soup on.'

k: Lovely afternoon.
src: 'Lovely afternoon.'

k: Two sweethearts lean toward each other. They have been leaning toward each other for forty years.
src: 'Two sweethearts lean toward each other. They have been leaning toward each other for forty years.'

k: Just KISS already.
src: 'Just KISS already.'

k: Let them have it, kid. Some moments are worth taking slow.
src: 'Let them have it, kid. Some moments are worth taking slow.'

k: Forty years is not slow, Corvin. Forty years is a medical condition.
src: 'Forty years is not slow, Corvin. Forty years is a medical condition.'

k: Three balls in the air above the juggler's hands. They never come down. They never go up, either.
src: 'Three balls in the air above the juggler\'s hands. They never come down. They never go up, either.'

k: That's the worst thing I've ever seen.
src: 'That\'s the worst thing I\'ve ever seen.'

k: Laaaaaaaaaaaaaa—
src: 'Laaaaaaaaaaaaaa—'

k: He is holding the first note of the Dawnsong. He has been holding it for forty years. He has not taken a breath.
src: 'He is holding the first note of the Dawnsong. He has been holding it for forty years. He has not taken a breath.'

k: Did you hear? The Keeper's little girl has been asking about the purple lights by the old wall. Such a curious child.
src: 'Did you hear? The Keeper\'s little girl has been asking about the purple lights by the old wall. Such a curious child.'

k: Somebody ought to keep an eye on her tonight.
src: 'Somebody ought to keep an eye on her tonight.'

k: Have you seen Miss Lysa? Her brother's looking all over.
src: 'Have you seen Miss Lysa? Her brother\'s looking all over.'

k: Miss Lysa! There you are, love. Your brother's been looking all over for you.
src: 'Miss Lysa! There you are, love. Your brother\'s been looking all over for you.'

k: I am not her.
src: 'I am not her.'

k: Miss Lysa! There you are, love.
src: 'Miss Lysa! There you are, love.'

k: Apples! Apples that never brown!
src: 'Apples! Apples that never brown!'

k: I'd eat one, only then there'd be one fewer. And I don't know how to grow more.
src: 'I\'d eat one, only then there\'d be one fewer. And I don\'t know how to grow more.'

k: Sel's been about to win since lunch. Never shows his hand.
src: 'Sel\'s been about to win since lunch. Never shows his hand.'

k: Somebody ought to call him. Not me. I'm comfortable.
src: 'Somebody ought to call him. Not me. I\'m comfortable.'

k: Squire Venn! Eyes front! You'll have the Lantern plaza tonight, lad, and the Keeper won't want a squire who fidgets.
src: 'Squire Venn! Eyes front! You\'ll have the Lantern plaza tonight, lad, and the Keeper won\'t want a squire who fidgets.'

k: Tonight. Ha. As if tonight's ever coming.
src: 'Tonight. Ha. As if tonight\'s ever coming.'

k: Can't ring her. Rope's stuck fast.
src: 'Can\'t ring her. Rope\'s stuck fast.'

k: You don't ring at noon, see. You ring at the turning of the hour. And the hour never turns.
src: 'You don\'t ring at noon, see. You ring at the turning of the hour. And the hour never turns.'

k: You're it! ...You're it! ...You're it!
src: 'You\'re it! ...You\'re it! ...You\'re it!'

k: I'm not it. I've never been it. I'm never going to be it.
src: 'I\'m not it. I\'ve never been it. I\'m never going to be it.'

k: Sundial
src: 'Sundial'

k: Books
src: 'Books'

k: Fountain
src: 'Fountain'

k: Bench
src: 'Bench'

k: The bell tower. Its great bell hangs at the top of the swing, about to fall back and ring the hour. It has been about to for forty years.
src: 'The bell tower. Its great bell hangs at the top of the swing, about to fall back and ring the hour. It has been about to for forty years.'

k: An anvil with a half-forged sword on it, still glowing. The smith's hammer hangs in the air just above it.
src: 'An anvil with a half-forged sword on it, still glowing. The smith\'s hammer hangs in the air just above it.'

k: ;_our
src: ';_our'

k: Lysa! LYSA!
src: 'Lysa! LYSA!'

k: She's not by the old wall. The lights are all over the plaza now. Please — please hurry.
src: 'She\'s not by the old wall. The lights are all over the plaza now. Please — please hurry.'

k: It's so pretty...
src: 'It\'s so pretty...'

k: Get indoors! The Lantern's guttering — the dark's coming up through the drains!
src: 'Get indoors! The Lantern\'s guttering — the dark\'s coming up through the drains!'

k: Hush, hush. Keep your eyes shut, sweetheart. If you don't look at it, it can't see you.
src: 'Hush, hush. Keep your eyes shut, sweetheart. If you don\'t look at it, it can\'t see you.'

k: Forty years I've walked this street, and I've never once seen the Lantern flicker.
src: 'Forty years I\'ve walked this street, and I\'ve never once seen the Lantern flicker.'

k: It's flickering.
src: 'It\'s flickering.'

k: Logbook
src: 'Logbook'

k: A chalk drawing on the flagstones: the sun, with a little door drawn in its side. Underneath, in a child's capitals: WHERE DOES IT GO?
src: 'A chalk drawing on the flagstones: the sun, with a little door drawn in its side. Underneath, in a child\'s capitals: WHERE DOES IT GO?'

k: A child's white shoe, the buckle undone. It is facing the wall, as if whoever wore it walked straight on without it.
src: 'A child\'s white shoe, the buckle undone. It is facing the wall, as if whoever wore it walked straight on without it.'

k: Here the old city wall is thinnest. The stones don't meet. Through the cracks, violet light, and a sound like the sea a long way down.
src: 'Here the old city wall is thinnest. The stones don\'t meet. Through the cracks, violet light, and a sound like the sea a long way down.'

k: Lysa's ribbon, on the cobbles. When Sable reaches for it, it isn't there. It was never really there.
src: 'Lysa\'s ribbon, on the cobbles. When Sable reaches for it, it isn\'t there. It was never really there.'

k: Not yet. Everyone's by the fire. One last night first.
src: 'Not yet. Everyone\'s by the fire. One last night first.'

k: Not like this. We should catch our breath first.
src: 'Not like this. We should catch our breath first.'

k: ← PORT GALE · WHISPERWOLD →nThe Gale Coast Road. Mind the cliffs. Mind the wind. Mind the cliffs in the wind.
src: '← PORT GALE · WHISPERWOLD →\nThe Gale Coast Road. Mind the cliffs. Mind the wind. Mind the cliffs in the wind.'

k: THE WHISPERWOLD — 1 mile.nTravelers are advised not to answer the trees.nBy order of the Thistledown Reeve.
src: 'THE WHISPERWOLD — 1 mile.\nTravelers are advised not to answer the trees.\nBy order of the Thistledown Reeve.'

k: Cairn
src: 'Cairn'

k: BY ORDER OF THE LORD-COMMANDER: any person sheltering a girl of about sixteen years, black hair, pale complexion, is to report to the Dawnguard. REWARD.nnBelow it: LOST — GINGER CAT. ANSWERS TO "ADMIRAL". (DOES NOT ANSWER.) — Bettany, Fish Market.
src: 'BY ORDER OF THE LORD-COMMANDER: any person sheltering a girl of about sixteen years, black hair, pale complexion, is to report to the Dawnguard. REWARD.\n\nBelow it: LOST — GINGER CAT. ANSWERS TO "ADMIRAL". (DOES NOT ANSWER.) — Bettany, Fish Market.'

k: PORT GALE — Harbor of the Gale Coast.nEast: the Coast Road, the Whisperwold, Thistledown and Aurenne.
src: 'PORT GALE — Harbor of the Gale Coast.\nEast: the Coast Road, the Whisperwold, Thistledown and Aurenne.'

k: ...Is that his seal? On your letter? Oh, my. Oh, my. Then you are in good hands, child. The very best.
src: '...Is that his seal? On your letter? Oh, my. Oh, my. Then you are in good hands, child. The very best.'

k: ...A woman in Thistledown who teaches you to _change_ your Crest? Don't tease me. That's cruel.
src: '...A woman in Thistledown who teaches you to _change_ your Crest? Don\'t tease me. That\'s cruel.'

k: Ride
src: 'Ride'

k: Barrel
src: 'Barrel'

k: the Salt & Lantern
src: 'the Salt & Lantern'

k: ♪ _Go not to the Whisperwold, my love, where the old trees keep the dead..._ ♪
src: '♪ _Go not to the Whisperwold, my love, where the old trees keep the dead..._ ♪'

k: THISTLEDOWN — Est. by people who were tired of walking.nInn · Trading Post · The Sage (up the hill, knock loudly, duck).
src: 'THISTLEDOWN — Est. by people who were tired of walking.\nInn · Trading Post · The Sage (up the hill, knock loudly, duck).'

k: Forester
src: 'Forester'

k: Old Bethan's up the hill, past Tobble's beehives. Knock loudly. Then duck.
src: 'Old Bethan\'s up the hill, past Tobble\'s beehives. Knock loudly. Then duck.'

k: ...Bread, I suppose. Fair enough. Still.
src: '...Bread, I suppose. Fair enough. Still.'

k: ...You've been up to see the heretic, haven't you? I can tell. You have that look. That _awake_ look.
src: '...You\'ve been up to see the heretic, haven\'t you? I can tell. You have that look. That _awake_ look.'

k: the Sleepy Thistle
src: 'the Sleepy Thistle'

k: kd":
EAST — AURENNE, 2 days.nNORTH — THE OLD QUARRY (CLOSED. BY ORDER OF RED TAM. SIGNED, RED TAM.)nWEST — THISTLEDOWN.
src: 'EAST — AURENNE, 2 days.\nNORTH — THE OLD QUARRY (CLOSED. BY ORDER OF RED TAM. SIGNED, RED TAM.)\nWEST — THISTLEDOWN.'

src: 'Hedge'

k: Listen
src: 'Listen'

k: Gravestone
src: 'Gravestone'

k: A standing stone, carved with spirals worn almost smooth. Moss has grown into the shape of a hand.
src: 'A standing stone, carved with spirals worn almost smooth. Moss has grown into the shape of a hand.'

k: Read
src: 'Read'

k: Lost something already? Should've minded your purse. I did say.
src: 'Lost something already? Should\'ve minded your purse. I did say.'

k: ...I was going to say.
src: '...I was going to say.'

k: Low Town folk keep asking the Watch about missing children. The Captain says Low Town is always losing people.
src: 'Low Town folk keep asking the Watch about missing children. The Captain says Low Town is always losing people.'

k: Says that's what Low Town is _for._ I didn't laugh. He noticed.
src: 'Says that\'s what Low Town is _for._ I didn\'t laugh. He noticed.'
